newsitem.title: UK: Stg strength could knock 1/4 point off UK GDP - CBI.
newsitem.headline: Stg strength could knock 1/4 point off UK GDP - CBI.

text.p: The Confederation of British Industry (CBI) said continued sterling strength could knock around 1/4 percentage point off GDP growth in 1997.
"If sterling remains at around 91.7 on a trade-weighted basis, it will impact on 1997 GDP growth by a little bit," said Sudhir Junankar, associate director of economic analysis.
"I imagine it would take around a quarter percentage point off GDP growth, making it 2.75 percent instead of 3.1 percent."
Sterling's trade-weighted index was 92.8 on Thursday.
Junankar said that when the CBI made its forecast of 3.1 percent growth next year, it assumed sterling would fall to around 89 on a trade-weighted basis.
